summary: Elena France Hanson is a scholar in Buddhist and religious studies. She earned her PhD at Harvard University under the supervision of Charles Hallisey (attested 1998).

Elena Mucciarelli works in Indology and religious studies. Educated at the University of Tübingen, she held a post there (2016–2017) before becoming Assistant Professor for Hinduism in the Sanskrit Tradition and Gonda Lecturer at the University of Groningen in 2020.

Eli Franco specializes in Indology, philosophy, and Buddhist studies. After earning his doctorate under Charles Malamoud and completing his Habilitation at Hamburg, he held posts at La Trobe, the Austrian Academy of Sciences, Leipzig (2004–2021), and Vienna.

Elijah Sacvan Ary is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Sera Monastery, INALCO, and Harvard University (~2001–2007), completing his PhD under Janet Gyatso and Leonard van der Kuijp.

Eliot Deutsch was a philosopher and Indologist who earned his PhD from Columbia University (1956–1960). He held posts at Rensselaer Polytechnic Institute (1960–1967) and the University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa (1967–2006), and edited Philosophy East and West.

Elisa Freschi is an Indologist and philosopher who earned her doctorate under Raffaele Torella. She held positions at Sapienza University of Rome, the University of Vienna, the Institute for the Cultural and Intellectual History of Asia, and the University of Toronto.
Elisa Ganser is an Indologist attested in 2026 as a Lektorin at the Göttingen Academy of Sciences and Humanities and a visiting researcher at the University of Zurich.

Elisabeth Schüssler Fiorenza is a religious studies scholar who studied at Würzburg and Münster. She held professorships at the University of Notre Dame (1970–1984), Episcopal Divinity School (1984–1988), and Harvard University (from 1988), and founded the SBL.

Elizabeth A. Cecil is a scholar of Indology, religious studies, and history/archaeology. She completed her PhD at Brown University under James L. Fitzgerald and has held posts at Leiden University and Florida State University (attested 2021).

Elizabeth De Michelis works in religious studies and Indology. She earned an MA from SOAS and a PhD from the University of Cambridge (~1996–2001), where she was director in 2000, and held a post at Oxford.
Elizabeth English works in Buddhist studies and Indology. She completed her PhD at the University of Oxford in 1999 under the doctoral supervision of Alexis Sanderson.

Elizabeth Errington specializes in history, archaeology, Indology, and Buddhist studies. After studies at SOAS under Adrian David Hugh Bivar, she served as curator of South and Central Asian pre-Islamic coins at the British Museum from 1993.

Elizabeth Guthrie is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies who earned her PhD from the University of Canterbury in 1994 and served as a tutor in religious studies at the University of Otago (~2006).

Elizabeth J. Harris specializes in Buddhist and religious studies. She earned her doctorate under Ananda Guruge and Yakupitiyage Karunadasa at the Postgraduate Institute of Pali and Buddhist Studies, holding posts at Westminster College (~1993–1996) and Birmingham (~2018).

Elizabeth J. Perry is a scholar in sinology and history/archaeology who studied at the University of Michigan (~1969–1978). She has held academic posts at the University of Washington (~1982–1990) and Harvard University (~1997).

Elizabeth Morrison works in Buddhist studies and sinology. She completed her doctoral studies under Bernard Faure and Carl Bielefeldt, and held academic posts at Amherst College (1998–1999) and Middlebury College (attested 2008).

Elizabeth Napper is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who earned her PhD at the University of Virginia under Paul Groner. She served as co-director of the Tibetan Nuns Project (attested 2001–2006).
Elizabeth Stuart is a religious studies scholar who founded Theology & Sexuality and served as Direktorin at the University of Winchester in 2021.

Elke Rogersdotter works in history/archaeology and Indology. She earned her PhD at Umeå University (attested 2006) under doctoral supervisor Thomas B. Larsson, supervisor Bozena Werbart, and co-advisors Karin Viklund and P. Ajithprasad.

Ellen M. Raven is a scholar of Indology and history/archaeology. She held posts at Leiden University (attested 2003, 2018) and served on the editorial board of Gonda Indological Studies (attested 2018).
